results.title: Ghana engages US civil rights lawyer Ben Crump over killings of nationals
results.content: The Ministry of Foreign Affairs has approved the engagement of prominent US civil rights lawyer Ben Crump to assist Ghana in seeking justice for nationals killed in the United States in recent months. In a statement issued on Tuesday, November 10, 2026, the Ministry said Ghana’s Permanent Mission in New York had been authorised to engage Mr Crump’s services at no cost to the Ghanaian taxpayer. “Approval has been granted to Ghana's Permanent Mission in New York to engage the services of celebrated US civil rights lawyer, Ben Crump, at no cost to the Ghanaian taxpayer, to assist Ghana in securing justice for all Ghanaians killed in the US in recent months,” the statement said. The Ministry said the decision reflected the government’s commitment to protecting the rights and dignity of Ghanaians living abroad.

results.title: KNUST Researcher investigates how AI can improve brain scan analysis
results.content: How well can artificial intelligence developed using medical data from Europe and North America analyse brain scans from Ghanaian patients? This question took Ghanaian biomedical engineer Dr Prince Ebenezer Adjei to the German Cancer Research Center (DKFZ) in Heidelberg, where he worked with researchers to investigate how medical imaging AI tools perform on Ghanaian clinical scans. Dr Adjei, who leads the Global Health AI Lab (GHAiC-K) at the Global Health and Infectious Diseases Group of the Kumasi Centre for Collaborative Research in Tropical Medicine (GHID-KCCR), has returned from the research visit with early findings that could inform the development of medical AI tools for Ghanaian healthcare. results.title: Minerals Commission CEO calls for prosecution of Chinese nationals involved in illegal mining
results.content: The Chief Executive Officer of the Minerals Commission, Isaac Andrews Tandoh, has called for the strict enforcement of Ghana’s mining laws against Chinese nationals and companies involved in illegal mining, saying foreign investors must be held accountable regardless of their nationality. Speaking at the China-Ghana Mining Cooperation Conference 2026, Mr Tandoh said Ghana’s mining regulations applied equally to all operators and that no foreign national or investor should be shielded from sanctions for breaking the law. He said a proposed framework agreement between Ghana and China was expected to strengthen cooperation in enforcing mining regulations and prosecuting Chinese nationals found engaging in illegal activities.

results.title: Ghana’s lithium future: Will local communities get a fair share?
results.content: Ghana's ambition to become a lithium producer is entering a new phase as Chinese mining giant Zhejiang Huayou Cobalt moves closer to gaining control of Atlantic Lithium, the company behind the country's first proposed commercial lithium mine. The development is raising questions about what the country and communities hosting the mine stand to gain, particularly as concerns over compensation and environmental responsibility emerge from the company's operations elsewhere. The questions come after a subsidiary of Huayou was ordered by authorities in the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) to pay US$6 million in compensation to three communities affected by an industrial wastewater spill. Congo Dongfang International Mining, a Huayou subsidiary, was ordered to pay US$2 million each to Kasapa, Kamatete and Kamisepe following a November 2025 incident at its Lubumbashi operation.

results.title: Ghana’s black gold and the quest for value
results.content: The modern era of Ghana's petroleum industry began with the establishment of the Ghana National Petroleum Corporation (GNPC) in 1983 under the Ghana National Petroleum Corporation Act (PNDCL 64). The GNPC was mandated to lead the nation's efforts to explore oil and gas resources efficiently. For decades, the sector saw exploratory efforts that eventually culminated in major commercial discoveries, transforming Ghana into a notable player in the West African energy market and requiring a robust, multi-tiered regulatory framework to manage the newfound wealth. The Jubilee Milestone While exploration began in the late 19th century, the watershed moment arrived in 2007 with the discovery of the Jubilee Field deep waters off the coast of the Western Region. results.title: Ghanaian startup launches SMS-based AI platform to reach young people without internet access
results.content: A Ghanaian technology startup, Scopeg AI, is partnering with the Ministry of Youth Development and Empowerment to expand access to artificial intelligence through an SMS-based platform designed for people without internet access or smartphones. The platform, Funza AI, allows users to interact with artificial intelligence by sending text messages to a short code and receiving AI-generated responses within seconds. It is designed to work on basic mobile phones, including feature phones, across mobile networks without requiring an internet connection or data bundle. The initiative is intended to make AI-powered services more accessible to young people, students, farmers, small business owners and jobseekers who may otherwise be excluded by the cost of internet access and digital devices.
